fields.statement: A full cycle of build runs is fast and rarely fails: afk's shipit/forge prompts are Rhiza's shipped defaults, guards stop the mechanical misses that cost retries, landing and merging main cost no full CI round, and known errors no longer hold runs, so rework halves and a ship-change run takes 40 minutes or less.

Every run role's shipped prompt carries afk's shipit/forge rules and checklists in Rhiza's words, one language-neutral guide topic per role on afk's six-section skeleton with shared blocks written once, and Rhiza's own repo runs them.

Runs stop the mechanical misses that cost a retry: a verifier, check or critic cannot say done without its record, builders and fixers run and report their checks before handing off, and no agent sleeps, polls or runs a command longer than about four minutes.

Rework is halved: over the 30 ship-change runs after the milestone, at most 15% of leaves need a second build attempt and at most 20% of runs need a second review cycle (baseline Nov 9-12: 31% and 42%).

A push that changes nothing outside .rhiza/ since the pull request's last green commit runs only the model checks, so landing a change set and merging model-only changes of main cost no full CI round.
Transient and known errors no longer hold runs: mean held time per ship-change run is at most 10 minutes over the 30 runs after the milestone (baseline Nov 9-12: about 24 minutes).

Median ship-change wall time is at most 40 minutes over the 30 runs after the milestone (baseline Nov 9-12: 55 minutes), measured by the perf analysis and recorded as Evidence, and the daemon journals why an accepted change set waits before its run starts.
Rhiza's own runs keep shipping through the change, and make check stays green.

fields.quote: Those should ship as the default build tools, and we also want to use them as our own.
fields.statement: afk's shipit/forge prompts become Rhiza's shipped default prompts for every run role, and Rhiza's own repo runs those defaults

Milestone 34 puts afk's prompts as shipped defaults and the guards first, then the CI-round cuts and the error sources behind held runs; the owner decides parallel leaves, a cheaper verifier model and the critic
